note: Question wording comes from the WP2 fact register; category titles verbatim from B2. Edit at the source and regenerate.

PRODUCT_KIND.question: Is what you place on the market hardware, software, or an online service?
PRODUCT_KIND.why_we_ask: The CRA covers products: hardware and software, including a cloud backend that your product needs in order to work. A purely online service with no product behind it is not covered.

legal_basis.quote: ‘product with digital elements’ means a software or hardware product and its remote data processing solutions
the absence of which would prevent the product with digital elements from performing one of its functions

options.label: Hardware, with or without its own software
Software that users install or run
A cloud service our own product needs in order to work
Only an online service, with no product of ours behind it

MARKET_STATUS.question: Where is the product in its life on the EU market?
MARKET_STATUS.why_we_ask: The CRA applies to products supplied on the EU market. If you plan to sell in the EU, we answer for the moment the product goes on sale. Showing a prototype at a fair, or using something only inside your own company, is not supplying it.

legal_basis.quote: This Regulation applies to products with digital elements made available on the market
the supply of a product with digital elements for distribution or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity

options.label: On sale or supplied in the EU
Planned for the EU market, not yet available
Only shown at trade fairs or demonstrations so far
Used only inside our own organisation
Not supplied in the EU, and not planned

COMMERCIAL_ACTIVITY.question: Is it supplied in the course of a commercial activity, whether paid or free of charge?
COMMERCIAL_ACTIVITY.why_we_ask: The CRA only covers products supplied as part of a business activity. Giving something away for free can still count: what matters is whether you earn from it in some way, for example by charging for support, for a platform around it, or by requiring users' personal data. Truly non-commercial projects, such as most volunteer open-source work, are outside.

legal_basis.quote: in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge

Supply in the course of a commercial activity might be characterised not only by charging a price for a product with digital elements, but also by charging a price for technical support services where this does not serve only the recuperation of actual costs, by an intention to monetise

DATA_INTERFACE_PRESENT.question: Does the product have any way to exchange data at all: network, radio, cable, USB, memory card, or a software interface?
DATA_INTERFACE_PRESENT.why_we_ask: The CRA covers products that can exchange data with something else. If your product has no way at all to exchange data (no network, radio, cable, USB, card slot or software interface), it is outside the CRA.

legal_basis.quote: includes a direct or indirect logical or physical data connection to a device or network
including through electrical, optical or mechanical interfaces, wires or radio waves

CONNECTION_INTENDED.question: Is the product intended to exchange data with another device or network, directly or indirectly?
CONNECTION_INTENDED.why_we_ask: What counts is whether exchanging data is part of how the product is meant to be used. It does not have to be the internet: a USB cable, Bluetooth, or a link through another device all count.

legal_basis.quote: the intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable use of which includes a direct or indirect logical or physical data connection to a device or network
a connection to a device or network, which does not take place directly but rather as part of a larger system

CONNECTION_FORESEEABLE.question: If no connection is intended, could one reasonably be foreseen in use?
CONNECTION_FORESEEABLE.why_we_ask: Even if you do not intend a connection, the CRA applies if users can reasonably be expected to connect the product anyway, for example through a port you have not disabled.

legal_basis.quote: the intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable use of which includes

EXCLUSION_SCREEN.question: Do any of these apply to the product? Tick all that apply, or none.
EXCLUSION_SCREEN.why_we_ask: Some products are covered by other EU laws instead of the CRA. Tick only what applies; each exclusion has its own condition, which the next question checks. If none applies, tick nothing.

legal_basis.quote: This Regulation does not apply to products with digital elements to which the following Union legal acts apply
This Regulation does not apply to spare parts

options.label: Medical or in vitro diagnostic device (Reg. 2017/745 or 2017/746)
Motor vehicle, or a system or component type-approved under Reg. 2019/2144
Two- or three-wheel vehicle or quadricycle (Reg. 168/2013), or a part for one
A spare part replacing an identical component
Made exclusively for national security or defence, or to process classified information
Other sector rules that we think cover cybersecurity
Excluded for another reason we cannot name

MEDICAL_STATUS.question: Is it CE-marked as a medical or in vitro diagnostic device, or does it have a medical purpose without being certified as one?
MEDICAL_STATUS.why_we_ask: Medical devices are excluded only if the medical device rules actually apply to them. A product with a medical purpose that is not certified as a medical device raises a question about those rules, which this tool cannot answer.

legal_basis.quote: (a) Regulation (EU) 2017/745; (b) Regulation (EU) 2017/746

options.label: CE-marked as a medical or in vitro diagnostic device
Has a medical purpose but is not certified as a medical device

VEHICLE_2019_2144.question: Is it a vehicle, system or component type-approved under Regulation (EU) 2019/2144?
VEHICLE_2019_2144.why_we_ask: Vehicles and their parts are excluded where the vehicle type-approval rules cover them. Equipment used to develop or test vehicles is not covered by those rules, so it stays under the CRA.

legal_basis.quote: (c) Regulation (EU) 2019/2144

options.label: Covered by a type approval under Reg. 2019/2144
A component; unclear whether that Regulation covers it
Not covered (for example equipment used to test vehicles)

AVIATION_2018_1139.question: Is it certified in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2018/1139?
AVIATION_2018_1139.why_we_ask: Aviation products are excluded only if they are actually certified under the EU aviation rules. Being the kind of product those rules cover is not enough.

legal_basis.quote: This Regulation does not apply to products with digital elements that have been certified in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2018/1139

options.label: Within its scope but not certified

MARINE_2014_90.question: Is it marine equipment within the scope of Directive 2014/90/EU?
MARINE_2014_90.why_we_ask: Marine equipment covered by the EU marine equipment rules is excluded from the CRA.

legal_basis.quote: This Regulation does not apply to equipment that falls within the scope of Directive 2014/90/EU

L_CATEGORY_168_2013.question: Is it a two- or three-wheel vehicle or quadricycle under Regulation (EU) No 168/2013, or a system or component for one? Is it an L1e vehicle designed to pedal?
L_CATEGORY_168_2013.why_we_ask: Mopeds, motorcycles, three-wheelers and quadricycles are excluded by a separate act. Light vehicles designed to be pedalled, such as speed pedelecs, are not excluded.

legal_basis.quote: However, that exclusion shall not apply to L1e category vehicles designed to pedal

options.label: Yes, an L-category vehicle or a part for one
An L1e vehicle designed to pedal, such as a speed pedelec

SPARE_PART.question: Is it a spare part replacing an identical component, made to the same specifications?
SPARE_PART.why_we_ask: A spare part that replaces an identical component, made to the same specifications, is excluded. A replacement with different or improved specifications is a product in its own right.

legal_basis.quote: spare parts that are made available on the market to replace identical components in products with digital elements and that are manufactured according to the same specifications as the components that they are intended to replace

options.label: Replaces an identical component, same specifications
A replacement with different or improved specifications

DEFENCE_STATUS.question: Was it developed or modified exclusively for national security or defence, or specifically designed to process classified information?
DEFENCE_STATUS.why_we_ask: Products made only for national security or defence are excluded. A product also sold for civilian use is not. Because this exclusion takes a product out of the CRA, you will need documents that show it.

legal_basis.quote: developed or modified exclusively for national security or defence purposes or to products specifically designed to process classified information

options.label: Exclusively for national security or defence
Specifically designed to process classified information

CORE_FUNCTION.question: In one sentence, what is this product for? What would a buyer say it does?
CORE_FUNCTION.why_we_ask: The class depends on what the product is for, not on every function it contains. A smartphone contains an operating system, but it is not an operating system. Describe your product as a buyer would; the following questions test what that means.

legal_basis.quote: Products with digital elements which have the core functionality of a product category set out in Annex III shall be considered to be important products

The integration of a product with digital elements which has the core functionality of a product category set out in Annex III shall not in itself render the product in which it is integrated subject to

STORES_PASSWORDS_CORE.question: Is storing passwords, on the device or on a server, what this product is for?
STORES_PASSWORDS_CORE.why_we_ask: Password managers are a listed category. What counts is whether storing passwords is the product's purpose, not whether it has a password field.

legal_basis.quote: Products with digital elements that store passwords, locally on a device or on a remote server

STORES_PASSWORDS_CORE.hint: Generating, sharing or auto-filling passwords is typical but not required.

PROTECTS_PHYSICAL_SECURITY.question: Is the product's purpose to protect the physical security of people in that setting?
PROTECTS_PHYSICAL_SECURITY.why_we_ask: Smart home security products are a listed category. What counts is whether the product's purpose is protecting people's physical security, for example against intruders. Watching pests, energy use or comfort does not count, even with a camera.

legal_basis.quote: protect the physical security of consumers in a residential setting

RESIDENTIAL_SETTING.question: Is it intended for use in a home, as opposed to an office, industrial or public setting?
RESIDENTIAL_SETTING.why_we_ask: The smart home categories cover products for people's homes. The same device sold for offices, shops or hotels falls outside them, though the CRA itself still applies.

legal_basis.quote: in a residential setting

CONTROL_PATH.question: How can the product be controlled or managed from another system?
CONTROL_PATH.why_we_ask: Smart home security products are covered when another system can control or manage them, such as an app over the internet or a home hub. Control only from a phone standing next to the device is a case the law does not clearly settle.

legal_basis.quote: can be controlled or managed remotely from other systems

options.label: From another system: an app over the internet, a hub or a cloud service
Only from a phone or device standing next to it (for example Bluetooth)

CENTRAL_CONTROL_OF_SECURITY.question: Does it centrally control products that protect physical security, such as locks or alarms?
CENTRAL_CONTROL_OF_SECURITY.why_we_ask: A hub or app that controls locks, alarms or security cameras in the home is in the same category as those products, even if it protects nothing itself.

legal_basis.quote: as well as hardware and software that centrally control such products

IC_TYPE.question: Is the product itself an integrated circuit? If so, which kind?
IC_TYPE.why_we_ask: Several categories cover chips: microprocessors, microcontrollers and custom chips with security functions, and secure elements. If your product is not itself a chip, all of them are ruled out with one answer.

legal_basis.quote: integrated circuits that carry out central processing functions integrating memory
integrated circuits that carry out central processing functions relying on external memory and peripherals

options.label: No, it is not itself a chip

SECURITY_FUNCTION.question: Does the product provide any security-related functionality, such as encryption, authentication, secure key storage, random number generation or a trusted execution environment?
SECURITY_FUNCTION.why_we_ask: Chips are only in these categories if they provide security functions such as encryption, authentication, secure key storage or random number generation.

legal_basis.quote: They additionally provide security-related functionalities, such as encryption, authentication, secure key storage, random number generation

SECURES_BEYOND_ITSELF.question: Does that security functionality aim to secure OTHER products, networks or services — beyond the chip itself?
SECURES_BEYOND_ITSELF.why_we_ask: A chip only counts if its security functions protect other products, networks or services, such as a secure boot chain for the device it sits in. Protecting only its own internal operation does not count.

legal_basis.quote: that aim to secure other products, networks or services beyond the microcontroller itself

TAMPER_PROTECTION.question: Does it provide tamper evidence, tamper resistance or tamper response?
TAMPER_PROTECTION.why_we_ask: Tamper evidence, resistance or response against physical attack moves a chip into a higher class, and is required for secure elements.

legal_basis.quote: including tamper evidence, resistance or response
Secure elements are microcontrollers or microprocessors with security-related functionalities, including tamper evidence, resistance or response

AVA_VAN_LEVEL.question: What AVA_VAN level is it designed to provide, under the Common Criteria?
AVA_VAN_LEVEL.why_we_ask: AVA_VAN is the Common Criteria rating for resistance to attack. Level 2 or 3 makes a tamper-resistant chip Class II; level 4 or higher makes it a secure element, which is critical. A certificate is good evidence; not having one proves nothing.

legal_basis.quote: designed to provide protection of AVA_VAN level 2 or 3
Secure elements are designed to provide protection of at least AVA_VAN.4

METERING_COMMUNICATION.question: Does it control communication between metering components and authorised third parties such as utilities?
METERING_COMMUNICATION.why_we_ask: Smart meter gateways are critical products. A gateway controls the communication between the metering system and outside parties such as the utility. A meter that only sends its own readings is not a gateway.

legal_basis.quote: control communication between components in or connected to smart metering systems

COLLECTS_METER_DATA.question: Does it collect, process and store meter data or personal data?
COLLECTS_METER_DATA.why_we_ask: A smart meter gateway collects, processes and stores meter data or personal data. This is one of five functions that together make a gateway.

legal_basis.quote: collect, process and store meter or personal data

CRYPTO_SUPPORT.question: Does it protect data and information flows by supporting specific cryptographic needs, such as encrypting and decrypting data for the metering system?
CRYPTO_SUPPORT.why_we_ask: A smart meter gateway protects the metering system's data by encrypting and decrypting it. Using encryption only for the device's own connection is not this function.

legal_basis.quote: protect data and information flows by supporting specific cryptographic needs, such as encryption and decryption of data

CRYPTO_SUPPORT.hint: This is about protecting the metering system's data flows, not only the device's own connection.

FIREWALLING.question: Does it incorporate firewalling functionality for the metering system?
FIREWALLING.why_we_ask: A smart meter gateway filters and restricts traffic for the metering system, like a firewall.

legal_basis.quote: incorporate firewalling functionalities

CONTROLS_OTHER_DEVICES.question: Does it provide the means to control other devices?
CONTROLS_OTHER_DEVICES.why_we_ask: A smart meter gateway lets the metering system control other devices. A device that only measures and reports controls nothing.

legal_basis.quote: provide the means to control other devices

METERED_COMMODITY.question: Which commodity does the metering system measure?
METERED_COMMODITY.why_we_ask: The gateway category names electricity, and gas or heat as other sources of energy. Water is not a source of energy, so a water gateway falls outside that part of the category.

legal_basis.quote: smart meter gateways related to smart metering systems measuring electricity
measuring consumption of other sources of energy such as gas or heat

options.label: Not part of a metering system

ADVANCED_SECURITY_CORE.question: Is the product's core functionality an advanced security purpose, such as secure cryptoprocessing, as opposed to a feature it also has?
ADVANCED_SECURITY_CORE.why_we_ask: The critical category also mentions other devices for advanced security purposes, such as secure cryptoprocessing, but the EU has not described them further. If your product's purpose is of that kind, the tool will flag it for expert review instead of deciding.

legal_basis.quote: other devices for advanced security purposes, including for secure cryptoprocessing

HIGH_RISK_AI_BASIS.question: Is the product a high-risk AI system under the AI Act, and on which basis?
HIGH_RISK_AI_BASIS.why_we_ask: If your product is also a high-risk AI system, the AI Act can change which conformity procedure you use. The dates differ by basis, and for machinery the AI Act was changed in 2026 in a way the CRA does not yet reflect.

legal_basis.quote: the relevant conformity assessment procedure provided for in Article 43

legal_basis.cite: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 2(2) and Art. 113(c), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
legal_basis.ref: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 2(2) and Art. 113(c), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744

options.label: High-risk under Annex III of the AI Act
High-risk because of a product law in Annex I, Section A, of the AI Act
High-risk because of a product law in Annex I, Section B (for example machinery)

EHR_SYSTEM.question: Is the product classified as an electronic health record (EHR) system under Regulation (EU) 2025/327?
EHR_SYSTEM.why_we_ask: Electronic health record systems follow the conformity procedure of the European Health Data Space rules instead of the CRA's own procedure, from 26 March 2027.

UNITS_PLACED_ON_MARKET.question: When are, or were, the units you are assessing placed on the market? Each unit counts on its own.
UNITS_PLACED_ON_MARKET.why_we_ask: The CRA's main requirements apply to units placed on the market from 11 December 2027. Units placed earlier are exempt unless they are substantially changed later. This is about the units you are asking about, not when the model was launched: later units of an older model must comply.

legal_basis.quote: Products with digital elements that have been placed on the market before 11 December 2027 shall be subject to the requirements set out in this Regulation only if, from that date, those products are subject to a substantial modification
This Regulation shall apply from 11 December 2027

UNITS_PLACED_ON_MARKET.hint: If you are asking about both stock already shipped and future production, assess them separately.

CHANGE_AT.question: When was the change made, or when will it be?
CHANGE_AT.why_we_ask: Only changes made from 11 December 2027 can bring earlier units under the main requirements.

legal_basis.quote: only if, from that date, those products are subject to a substantial modification

CHANGE_AFFECTS_PURPOSE.question: Does that change modify the intended purpose for which the product was assessed?
CHANGE_AFFECTS_PURPOSE.why_we_ask: A change that alters what the product is meant to be used for is a substantial modification, and brings the product under the CRA's main requirements.

legal_basis.quote: which results in a modification to the intended purpose for which the product with digital elements has been assessed

CHANGE_AFFECTS_ANNEX_I.question: Does the change affect how secure the product is — for example how it authenticates users, protects stored or transmitted data, or delivers updates?
CHANGE_AFFECTS_ANNEX_I.why_we_ask: A change that affects whether the product still meets the CRA's security requirements is also a substantial modification. That needs a security assessment, which this tool cannot do, so a change of this kind is flagged for review.

legal_basis.quote: which affects the compliance of the product with digital elements with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I of Annex I

RADIO_EQUIPMENT_RED_DA.question: Is the product radio equipment that (a) can communicate over the internet, directly or via other equipment; (b) is internet-connected or in the childcare, toy or wearable categories AND can process personal data, traffic data or location data; or (c) is internet-connected and lets the user transfer money, monetary value or virtual currency?
RADIO_EQUIPMENT_RED_DA.why_we_ask: Before the CRA applies, radio products may already have cybersecurity rules under the radio equipment rules: since 1 August 2025, for internet-connected radio equipment, equipment handling personal data, and equipment that can transfer money.

legal_basis.quote: radio equipment that can communicate itself over the internet

OTHER_LEGISLATION_CERTIFICATE.question: Does the product hold an EU type-examination certificate or approval decision covering cybersecurity under other EU harmonisation legislation? If so, when does it expire?
OTHER_LEGISLATION_CERTIFICATE.why_we_ask: If your product already holds an EU type-examination certificate covering cybersecurity under other EU product rules, that certificate stays valid for a while under the CRA.

legal_basis.quote: shall remain valid until 11 June 2028, unless they expire before that date

CERTIFICATE_EXPIRY.question: When does that certificate expire?
CERTIFICATE_EXPIRY.why_we_ask: The certificate stays valid until 11 June 2028, or until its own expiry date if that comes first.

legal_basis.quote: shall remain valid until 11 June 2028, unless they expire before that date

ASSESSMENT_DATE.question: Assessment date
ASSESSMENT_DATE.why_we_ask: Which obligations already apply depends on the date of the assessment.
